paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the God who calls you to leave is the same God who goes with you. He says, "I am the first, and I am the last," and that His own hand founded the earth (Isaiah 48:12-13). No idol saw Babylon's fall coming, and He did (Isaiah 48:14-15). So when He says "Leave Babylon!" you can trust the One who said it (Isaiah 48:20).

Now here's the heavy part, and I think it hurts a little. He says, "If only you had paid attention to My commandments, your peace would have been like a river" (Isaiah 48:18). He's the One who "teaches you for your benefit" and "directs you in the way you should go" (Isaiah 48:17). His commands aren't Him being bossy, friend. They're a Redeemer showing you the road to peace, and I wish I'd listened that fast to my oven timer.

So what do you do with that? You listen, and you go where He points, even when staying put feels comfy. He led His people through the deserts, and they did not thirst, because He split the rock and water gushed out (Isaiah 48:21). He keeps His word, and He is the Redeemer, as the shout of joy says: "The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!" (Isaiah 48:20). Then comes the closing line, "There is no peace," says the LORD, "for the wicked" (Isaiah 48:22), which tells me real peace comes from walking with Him and not away from Him.
